result.title: How Many, but How Sure? Class Competition as a Confidence Proxy in Multi-Class Density-Based Counting
result.comment: 2+1 pages, 1 figure; a 2027 Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference abstract
result.summary: Multi-class density estimators can count objects in crowded scenes, but their class-wise outputs offer no indication of how reliably density mass has been allocated. We introduce a training-free confidence proxy based on local competition between the strongest class channels. The resulting prominence measure requires only the predicted density maps, with no retraining or access to model internals. We test whether residual competition is diagnostic of cross-class leakage by attenuating contested density at inference time. On DSACA predictions for the Hicks et al. dataset, this reduces overall MAE from 0.920 to 0.846, suggesting that class competition contains useful information about count reliability.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种免训练的置信度代理：用多类密度图中最强类别通道之间的局部竞争得到 prominence 度量，并检验残余竞争是否指示跨类泄漏——在推理时衰减存在竞争处的密度，使 DSACA 在 Hicks 数据集上的 MAE 从 0.920 降至 0.846。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把内部类间竞争当作可靠性信号并做推理期干预，可能启发 LVR 中对「当前 latent 状态是否可信、何时继续 LOOK 或 STOP」的置信度评估，可供核查；但其对象是密度计数而非多模态推理，联系较间接。
